english: the verb, then what it acts on, then where, from whom or for whom; a long "who" clause may trail at the end, its word kept by the verb
example: he's taken everyone from us who believes, never "he's taken from us everyone who believes"

english: a short adverb after the first auxiliary or modal, never between two verbs where it could belong to either
example: would then deliver, never "who came then would deliver"

shape: relative clause led by its preposition
english: a plain phrase or a clause with its preposition at the end, as *a cui tans* is "the king of that time"
example: the king of that time, never "the one in whose time they come"

shape: purpose said as making someone sure
english: so you can be sure, as *pour toi faire plus certain que* is said
example: so you can be sure God has given me this wisdom, never "to make you surer of the understanding God has granted me"

shape: bare after closing a span of time
english: the span, then "later", or the moment's own turn, "the next day", "a week after he left"
example: he died three days later, never "he lived only three days after"

shape: duty closed on a bare have
english: the duty said as the charge it is and the comparison said in full, as *se jou l'eusse aussi a querre que vous avés* is said
example: if I'd been sent to find him, as you were, never "if I'd had to search the way you have"

english: the reason opened on "because" or "since", or set after a colon
example: never believe me again, because I know his end well, never "never believe me again, for I know his end well"

english: I want you to know, "you can be sure" or "believe me", as *sachiés que* is said
example: you can be sure they'll land in three months, never "know that they'll land in three months"

shape: a bare title as an address
english: my lady from one who serves her, otherwise her name or nothing; a speech to a group opens on what is said
example: My lady, Uther sends you this, never "Lady, Uther sends you this"
